The book draws on the former director's professional experience and her upbringing, particularly the practical intelligence and collaborative strategies she observed in her late parents.
The post NNPC ex-director launches book on failure of family businesses appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Tsohon difekta na NNPC ya bugi littafi game da gazawar kasuwancin iyali. Littafin ya dogara da ƙwarewar aiki ta tsohon difekta da kakarinsa, musamman ƙarfin hankali da dabarun aiki da ta gani a wurin iyalarta masu gida.
critical_questions: What specific failures in family businesses does the book address, and are these based on empirical research or primarily anecdotal observations from the author's family?
Who stands to benefit commercially from this book launch, and does the author have undisclosed financial interests in family business consulting or advisory services?
Why is an NNPC ex-director's personal family experience being positioned as authoritative commentary on family business failure, and what credentials qualify her in this domain?
Are there contrary voices or alternative perspectives from successful family business operators included in the book, or does it present a one-sided narrative?
What is the timing significance of this book launch - is it connected to any current policy discussions on family businesses or NNPC-related controversies?

articles.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, others
articles.summary:
Governor Mbah highlighted his administration's investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, and revival of moribund assets
The post 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, others appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: 2027: APC ya bugi jarin yakin niyyar zabe a Nsukka, ta yi alkawari na isar da Mbah, Tinubu, da sauransu
critical_questions: What specific infrastructure and security projects has Governor Mbah completed, and are there independent verification reports or audit findings?
Why is the APC campaign flagging off for 2027 elections this early, and what funding sources are being used for this campaign launch?
Who are the 'others' being promised delivery, and what constituencies do they represent - is there potential patronage or factional politics at play?
Are the claimed achievements in healthcare and education backed by measurable data, or are these largely rhetorical assertions?
What voices from opposition parties or independent analysts are absent from this coverage, and does the article present competing claims about Mbah's tenure?

articles.title: Abiodun orders immediate reconstruction of Saje-Elega-Adedotun Road
articles.summary:
The governor said the reconstruction was part of his administration’s commitment to upgrading infrastructure and giving Abeokuta, the state capital, a befitting facelift.
The post Abiodun orders immediate reconstruction of Saje-Elega-Adedotun Road appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Abiodun ya umarta na kauri sake gina titin Saje-Elega-Adedotun. Gwamna ya ce ginin ya kasance part na niyyar gwamnatinsa na haɓaka abubuwan harkokin gida da ba wa Abeokuta, babbar gida na jihar, kyakkyawan sura.
critical_questions: What is the current condition of the road and why has reconstruction been delayed until now?
What is the budget allocation for this project and has it been publicly disclosed for accountability?
Who are the contractors awarded this project and what are their track records on previous government contracts?
Why does the article lack specific timelines, completion dates, or measurable deliverables for this 'immediate reconstruction'?
Are there competing infrastructure needs in other parts of Ogun State, and how was this particular road prioritized over them?

articles.title: Six climate measures could save 1.6 million lives yearly – WHO
articles.summary:
According to the report, the six interventions could prevent one in every 40 deaths globally, based on modelled projections, while avoiding 16.7 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.
The post Six climate measures could save 1.6 million lives yearly – WHO appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Matakan jiya gida shida za su iya ceton rayuka miliyan 1.6 a shekara - WHO
critical_questions: Which specific six climate interventions are referenced, and who determines their feasibility and cost-effectiveness across different economic contexts?
What are the assumptions underlying these mortality projections, and have independent researchers peer-reviewed these modelled estimates?
Whose voices are missing from this report - particularly from developing nations that bear climate impacts but lack resources to implement these measures?
Who benefits most from promoting these six specific measures, and are there competing climate solutions being deprioritized by this framing?
What is the timeline for implementation, and does the WHO address who funds and enforces these interventions in low-income regions?

articles.title: Lessons Plateau can learn from US Policy of Citizenship
articles.summary: Plateau State has lived for decades with a question America answered over 150 years ago: Who is a citizen, and who is a stranger? In Jos North, Bassa, Barkin-Ladi and Riyom, the distinction between “indigene” and “settler” has decided who gets a job, who gets a school admission, who gets a certificate, and in extreme […]
articles.hausa_translation: Abubuwan da Plateau zai iya koyi daga Manufar Jama'a ta Amurka - Plateau State ya kasance tsawon shekaru da tambaya da Amerika ta amsa fiye da shekaru 150 da suka wuce: Wane ne jama'a, kuma wane ne baaje? A Jos North, Bassa, Barkin-Ladi da Riyom, bambanci tsakanin 'yan gida' da 'bakin bayi' ya yanke shawo a kan wanda zai sami aiki, wanda zai sami karatu, wanda zai sami takardar karantarwa, kuma a mamaye.
critical_questions: Who benefits from perpetuating the indigene/settler distinction in Plateau State's employment and education systems, and what economic or political interests does it serve?
Why is the US citizenship model being presented as a solution when Nigeria's 1999 Constitution already has provisions on citizenship—and what specific policy gaps is this article overlooking?
Whose voices are missing from this narrative—particularly settlers' accounts of discrimination and indigenes who support equal rights?
Does the comparison to US policy obscure that America's citizenship framework has its own ongoing inequities (systemic racism, immigration restrictions), potentially offering false equivalence?
What evidence supports that adopting US-style citizenship policy would actually resolve Plateau's intercommunal conflicts, versus masking deeper resource and land disputes?

articles.title: NMDPRA, EFCC seal off Chinese-linked illegal refinery in Ogun
articles.summary: Officials of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday raided an illegal refinery linked to the Chinese at Ogere-Remo, Ikenne Local Government Area of Ogun State. The officials stormed the facility after the EFCC’s intelligence exposed what investigators described as a well-fenced, crude
articles.hausa_translation: Jami'an NMDPRA da EFCC sun rufe gida mai shuni da ake danganta da Sinawa a Ogun
critical_questions: What evidence directly links this facility to Chinese nationals, and who benefits from emphasizing this foreign connection?
Why was this particular refinery targeted now, and were similar domestic-linked operations raided with equal enforcement vigor?
What happens to seized assets and crude oil, and where does the recovered value go in the enforcement chain?
How extensive is this illegal refining operation, and what is the scale compared to other unreported sites in the region?
Who provided the EFCC intelligence, and could commercial competitors or political actors have motivated this specific raid?

It was learnt that past leaders of both labour centres had held a crucial meeting before calling on the two warring parties to […]
articles.hausa_translation: Kwanciyar N70,000: Tsofaffin jagoran aiki sun shiga cikin rigimar NLC da TUC
critical_questions: What specific incidents or policy disagreements triggered the NLC-TUC rift that ex-leaders are now attempting to mediate?
Who benefits most from a reconciliation between these labour bodies - workers, government, or union leadership consolidating power?
Why are former leaders taking initiative rather than current leadership resolving this independently, and what influence do they actually wield?
Is the N70,000 allowance mention connected to the dispute, or is it separate context being used to frame the reconciliation narrative?
What do rank-and-file workers know about this rift, and are their voices represented in the reconciliation efforts being described?

articles.title: UCL: Gyokores leads Arsenal to victory in Prague as Como claim historic 9-1 win
articles.summary: Viktor Gyokores scored and assisted Noni Madueke in Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday night. The Swede was in the mood to prove head coach Mikel Arteta wrong for his lack of playing time, and he produced the goods for the scrappy win. Gyokores sent Madueke clear for […]
articles.hausa_translation: Viktor Gyokores ya zaa kwallo kuma ya taimaka wa Noni Madueke a cikin Arsenal's nasara 2-1 a kan Slavia Prague a UEFA Champions League jiya. Swediyan nan ya nuna karfin sa don tabbatar da kansa ga koche Mikel Arteta game da rashin lokacin wasa, kuma ya aiwatar da aikinsa sosai.
critical_questions: Why does the headline credit Gyokores but the summary indicates Arsenal had 'scrappy' play - does the performance justify the triumphalism?
Is the framing of Gyokores 'proving wrong' Arteta's selection choices legitimate analysis or narrative speculation without supporting evidence?
Why is a 2-1 victory described as 'historic' for Como's 9-1 win when these appear to be separate matches - is this editorial error or misleading conflation?
What is the source's ownership interest in Arsenal coverage, and does the tone reflect standard sports journalism or promotional bias?
Are specific statistics (possession, shots, chances) absent from this summary, and if so, does that weaken the credibility of performance assessment?
